run.question:
The checkout-service in production-us-east-2 is throwing 500 errors right
now. Investigate the root cause using app-269-prod-logs.

report.summary: The 500-level failures of checkout-service in production-us-east-2 are evidenced in app-269-prod-logs: at 2026-11-21T04:42:57Z checkout-service logged 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' while payment-service (same cluster field production-us-east-2) logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at the same second; at 05:42:57Z checkout-service logged 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' and at 06:12:57Z 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open'. Read as a chain, the failing outbound call to the external provider stripe-us is the deepest cause the logs support; payment-service failures then opened checkout-service's circuit breaker, which is what the later checkout failures cite. The same index also holds two production-eu-west-2 documents (checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms', payment-service 'Adyen-eu healthy'); those describe a different cluster and are not evidence about production-us-east-2. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable in this Run, so no error-rate, latency or call-chain confirmation exists; Kubernetes access is scoped to the other cluster (production-eu-west-2), so the us-east-2 payment-service/checkout-service pods, their previous-container logs, events, quotas and networkpolicies were not observed. Why stripe-us timed out is not explained by any available data. The app-269 namespace objects in the readable cluster (a freshly created nginx 'checkout-service' pod created 2026-11-21T06:42:54Z, with no Service and only nginx startup logs) are a different entity created after the incident and are not the failing checkout-service.

claims.text: The index app-269-prod-logs is the only index returned for pattern '*' (6 documents, 7.3kb) and maps the fields cluster, level, message, service and timestamp; the time field is timestamp, not @timestamp.

All 6 documents in app-269-prod-logs fall between 2026-11-21T04:42:57Z and 2026-11-21T06:12:57Z. checkout-service with cluster field production-us-east-2 logged level ERROR 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' at 2026-11-21T04:42:57Z.

payment-service with cluster field production-us-east-2 logged level ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 2026-11-21T04:42:57Z, the same second as checkout-service's payment-provider timeout log.

checkout-service with cluster field production-us-east-2 logged 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' at 2026-11-21T05:42:57Z and 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open' at 2026-11-21T06:12:57Z; these are checkout-service's own error lines naming payment-service as the failing dependency.

The same index contains two production-eu-west-2 documents: checkout-service level INFO 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' at 2026-11-21T04:42:57Z and payment-service level INFO 'Adyen-eu healthy' at 2026-11-21T06:12:57Z. Their cluster field is production-eu-west-2, so they describe a different cluster than the failing one.

In the Kubernetes cluster my access is scoped to (not production-us-east-2), namespace app-269 holds exactly one deployment, checkout-service, with image nginx:1.27-alpine, revision 1, 1/1 ready and Available=True with lastTransitionTime 2026-11-21T06:42:57Z; the pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-92j48 started 2026-11-21T06:42:54Z with 0 restarts and its container logs are only nginx startup notices with no error lines. No Service object exists in namespace app-269.

The only events in the authorized window are 6 Normal events on objects in namespace app-269 of the readable cluster (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet; Pod Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started; ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate), timestamped 2026-11-21T06:42:54Z to 06:42:57Z; they show a first-time rollout of that nginx deployment, not a crash, eviction or OOM.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (in the readable cluster's otel-demo namespace) declares fault-injection flags paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%', variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off) and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable', on/off), both state ENABLED with defaultVariant 'off'; the same ConfigMap carries Prometheus alerting rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh on traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name="checkout".

The otel-demo payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d in the readable cluster returned 99 log lines matching err|error|fail|timeout|exception|panic|stripe|charge between 05:43:41Z and 06:43:00Z, all of them info-level 'Charge request received.' entries with no error, timeout or stripe-related text shown.

The origin of the production-us-east-2 incident is the external payment provider stripe-us: its /v1/charges call did not answer within 30s, payment-service therefore failed charge requests (checkout later measured a 41% failure rate to payment-service), checkout-service's circuit breaker opened for payment-service, and subsequent POST /api/checkout calls failed with 'circuit-breaker open'. Why stripe-us timed out is not shown by any available data.

A fault-injection flag (paymentFailure or paymentUnreachable) could be switched on in the production-us-east-2 environment, which I cannot read; the only flagd configuration observed (otel-demo/flagd-config in the readable cluster) leaves both at defaultVariant 'off', so this remains an unverified candidate rather than an observed cause.

The production-eu-west-2 entries in the same index (checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' at 04:42:57Z, payment-service 'Adyen-eu healthy' at 06:12:57Z) and the healthy-looking eu-west-2 payment pod logs cannot be used to argue anything about production-us-east-2: a different cluster and a different provider (Adyen-eu vs stripe-us) are described.

The app-269/checkout-service deployment and pod in the readable cluster are not the failing checkout-service: that deployment is a single nginx:1.27-alpine container at revision 1, created 2026-11-21T06:42:54Z (after every us-east-2 error line), has no Service in app-269, 0 restarts and no error log lines, and its events are only first-rollout Normal events.

Obtain metrics and traces for production-us-east-2 (checkout PlaceOrder error ratio, payment charge error/latency, span status codes and the client span from payment-service to stripe-us) and read payment-service and checkout-service pod logs in that cluster, including previous-container logs and events, to confirm the log-only causal chain and to determine the provider-side failure mode.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable in this Run: get_all_labels, get_label_values, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so checkout/payment error-rate, latency and circuit-breaker metrics and any label coverage (including ERROR-status series) for production-us-east-2 are unobserved, not zero.

Jaeger was unavailable in this Run: traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level confirmation of the payment-service -> stripe-us call, its status or duration exists.

No Kubernetes access to production-us-east-2: my Kubernetes access reads only the other cluster (production-eu-west-2), so the us-east-2 checkout-service and payment-service pods, their container statuses, previous-container logs, events, resourcequotas, endpoints and networkpolicies were not checked.
stripe-us is an external payment provider with no telemetry in any available source; the reason for its >30s /v1/charges timeout and whether it is still failing are unknown.

The latest production-us-east-2 entry in app-269-prod-logs is 2026-11-21T06:12:57Z; there is no us-east-2 log sample after that, so whether the checkout failures persist to the end of the window (06:43:06Z) is unknown.
The runtime state of flagd flags (effective variants served to payment/checkout) cannot be read; only the ConfigMap defaults were observed, and secrets are not readable.
The change_history integration is not available, so any change that may have altered the stripe-us configuration or provider latency is unobserved.
next_steps: Check the stripe-us provider status/latency history and its /v1/charges error rate around 2026-11-21T04:42:57Z, and whether that provider call recovers after 06:12:57Z.
In production-us-east-2, read payment-service and checkout-service pod logs, previous-container logs and events, and check deployment/replica-set status for restarts during 04:42-06:43Z.

Once metrics are reachable, evaluate the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh expression (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_ERROR"}) and payment charge error/latency for the incident window.
Review the effective flagd flag values served in the production-us-east-2 environment for paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
